 Order

Petitioner a land owner is knocking at the doors of Writ Court for laying a challenge to the Preliminary Notification dated 15.05.2007 issued under Section 28(1) and the rejection of his Objections by the SLAO vide order dated 22.05.2022 passed under Section 28(3) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, 1966.

He has also laid challenge to the Notification dated 29.10.2013 issued u/s 4 of the Act whereby only a certain portion of his land has been left out from the 'industrial area' remaining having been retained therein.
2. After service of notice, the 1st Respondent - State is represented by the learned AGA; the 2nd Respondent - KIADB is represented by its Sr. Panel Counsel; and the 3rd Respondent - SEZ is represented by its Panel Counsel who has filed the Statement of Objections resisting the Writ Petition.
All the advocates appearing for the Respondents oppose the Writ Petition making submission in justification of the impugned orders and section 4 Notification.

3. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the Petition papers, this Court is inclined to grant a limited indulgence in the matter as under and for the following reasons:
a) The land of the Petitioner in all admeasures 50 cents; the same was notified for acquisition under Section 28(1) on 15.05.2007; it was followed by the Final Notification dated 28.05.2010 issued u/s 28(4) of the 1966 Act.

In Petitioner's W.P.No.25904/2010(LA-KIADB), a Coordinate Bench vide judgment dated 13.10.2011 having voided the Final Notification, permitted him to file Objections to the Preliminary Notification, which the Petitioner did by filing one.

The Land Acquisition Officer vide order dated 22.05.2012 has overruled the Objections without considering the requirement of the extent of land as specified by the 3rd Respondent Sri P Vittal Chowta vs The State Of Karnataka on 14 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19064478/

wherein, only a lesser extent of 12.84 cents has been sought for the formation of the road and not 28 cents, as notified.

It hardly needs to be stated that where the acquisition is at the instance of a beneficiary, the extent of the land cannot exceed the requisition, more particularly when the right to property is constitutionally guaranteed under Article 300A and such acquisition can be done only as a concession shown to the State that exercises the power of eminent domain.

b) There is absolutely no discussion in the impugned order passed by the SLAO under Section 28(3)
of the 1966 Act as to why 28 cents of land would be required by the beneficiary SEZ which has specified only 12.84 cents as being its requirement for the formation of quadrilateral road ("Zvx").
Thus, there is an error apparent on the face of the record which has enormous consequence on the property rights of the Petitioner.
The contention that the land owner would be granted compensation is a poor solace since men by their very nature have emotional attachment to the land & buildings.

c) There is force in the submission of learned Sr. Panel Counsel appearing for the 2nd Respondent - KIADB that the declaration of particular area as industrial area only under Sections 1 & 3 of the 1966 Act would not per se affect the property rights of the citizens and therefore, the Court should be slow in granting invalidation of such Notifications, more particularly when all aspects having been considered, the government has issued the subject Notification u/s 4 of the Act.
What prejudice would be caused to the Petitioner by his land being subsumed in an industrial area as notified by the government remains to be riddle wrapped in enigma.
In the absence of prejudice, the arguable lacunae in the State action would not warrant indulgence of the Writ Court.

In the above circumstances, a Writ of Certiorari issues quashing the impugned Preliminary Notification dated 28.05.2007 only to the extent that it notifies the land for acquisition in excess of 12.84 cents.
Petitioner agrees for the acquisition of the said extent of land and therefore, the impugned order dated 22.05.2012 is sustained only to that extent, the remaining having been set at naught.

Petitioner's consent for accomplishing the acquisition to the extent of 12.84 cents of his land having been placed on record, the subject acquisition be treated as having been done under Section 29(2) of the 1966 Act for all practical purposes.
It hardly needs to be stated that the delay in the payment of compensation shall not go with impunity.
No costs.
